parameters.content:
## Setup 1. Import this workflow, then open **Send Proposal Email** and attach a Gmail OAuth2 credential (connect the Google account that should send these — Google Cloud Console → enable the Gmail API → OAuth client → n8n's Gmail credential does the rest). 2. Open **Proposal Email Webhook** → Authentication is set to *Header Auth*. Create a new **Header Auth** credential (this is a regular credential, not an instance-level Variable — no admin/owner access needed): Name = `x-webhook-secret`, Value = any random string. 3. In the app's `.env`, set: - `EMAIL_PROVIDER=n8n` - `N8N_WEBHOOK_URL=` - `N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET=` 4. Activate the workflow. n8n's Webhook node checks the header itself before the workflow even starts — a request with the wrong or missing `x-webhook-secret` gets an automatic `403` and never reaches Send Proposal Email, so there's no separate "check secret" node to build (Variables aren't needed anywhere in this workflow). ## Why "Send a message", not "Send and Wait for Response" Gmail's *Send and Wait* operation pauses the workflow until the **recipient** replies or clicks a button in the email — meant for human-in-the-loop approval steps, not for confirming a send. This workflow is called synchronously from the app (`src/lib/email.ts`, `sendViaN8n`) with a 10-second timeout on the fetch, so anything that waits on the client would just time out on the app's side while n8n kept waiting indefinitely. If you want an approve/reject-by-email step for the *internal* approval gate (before a proposal is sent), that's a good fit for *Send and Wait* — but as a separate workflow triggered on `submitted_for_review`, not this one. ## Payload the app sends ```json { "to": "client@example.com", "clientName": "...", "companyName": "...", "salespersonName": "...", "proposalLink": "https://.../api/documents//download", "subject": "Proposal for ...", "html": "

...

", "text": "..." } ``` See `src/lib/email.ts` (`sendViaN8n`) in the app repo — this workflow is the other end of that call. ## Response contract The app only checks for a 2xx status to treat the send as successful, but this workflow always replies with a JSON body describing what happened, which shows up as `lastError` on the proposal if something goes wrong: - `200 { ok: true, provider: "n8n", messageId }` - `403` — wrong/missing secret (handled by the Webhook node itself, before this workflow's logic runs) - `502 { ok: false, error: "" }`

parameters.responseBody: ={{ { ok: false, error: ($json.error && $json.error.message) || $json.message || "Failed to send email" } }}
